title: Jurgen Klopp says Mohamed Salah ‘irreplaceable’ at Liverpool, discusses Sadio Mane relationship
content:
Jurgen Klopp says Mo Salah is “irreplaceable” as Liverpool prepare for life without their record-breaking Egyptian.

The former Liverpool manager has exchanged messages with Salah since the 33-year-old forward, who has scored 255 goals in 435 appearances for the club, announced earlier this week that he will leave at the end of the season.

“This specific kind of player is irreplaceable,” Klopp told reporters at a special LFC Foundation event ahead of Saturday’s charity match between Liverpool Legends and Borussia Dortmund Legends at Anfield.

“There will be a void that somebody will fill. But the specific player, Mo Salah? I’m not sure there is even another one existing out there. There are other people playing on that wing with different strengths, different qualities, but it is the numbers he produces – they’re unmatched from that position.

“You tell him he is a striker he says: ‘no, no, no, I am a winger!’ The numbers for a winger are ridiculous. For a striker they are pretty much unmatched. So, if it is impossible, why should you try?

“We lost Sadio Mane. We could sing a song about him. What a player he was! Bobby Firmino – Oh. My. God.

“On the day Gini (Wijnaldum) went, probably none of you thought ‘that’s a big miss’ until he was not there anymore and then you thought: ‘Oh! He was the combination of technique, power, tactical discipline and all these kind of things.’ But other players came in. Don’t try to chase the shadows. Find a new way and play.”

Salah’s heroics helped to inspire Liverpool to some of the greatest triumphs of the Klopp era as they celebrated both Champions League and Premier League glory together.

The current head of global soccer for Red Bull admits it was a “challenge” to manage Salah at times and there were ‘”arguments”, but any ill feeling never lingered.

“I heard that Mo was going to leave,” Klopp said. “Then I saw the video. I am already in a different perspective because I watch from the outside. So I text him what I thought in that moment. I can sum it up: ‘I am really happy and proud that I was part of the whole journey.’

“We both know that we had these arguments, not big, big arguments. Like the one at West Ham (April, 2024), both of us, five seconds later, would have thought: ‘No, we don’t do that in public, come on, rewind.’ Next morning it was already over but it happened in public.

“We never lost respect for each other and that is what I really like. He didn’t like me for a second when I took him off after 87 minutes and all these kind of things, and you think: ‘Why?’ The time with him and Sadio together, they were a challenge, of course they were. Special players are a challenge. Tell me one who is not? The real difference makers. The one who wasn’t by the way was Bobby Firmino!

“Now it’s time, not for Liverpudlians obviously because there is still a lot to go for, but for me it’s a bit different and I can already reflect. And what a time that was, and what a player he is. My God. The goals he scored and the games we had. In their prime, that team was incredible, in each and every part.

“My big target was always that when I am old and grey, I’m grey but maybe not that old, I could look back and smile, and that is definitely the case. The Mo movie is a beautiful movie, and to make it interesting you have to have a few edges. It’s a beautiful movie with a happy end.”

Klopp became an honorary ambassador for the LFC Foundation when he left the club in 2024. On Saturday he will be back in the Anfield dugout to assist Liverpool Legends manager Kenny Dalglish against another one of his former clubs, Dortmund.

Steven Gerrard, Thiago Alcantara, Pepe Reina, Peter Crouch, Sami Hyypia, Ryan Babel and Albert Riera will be among the Liverpool squad on duty.
